pages.subtitle: A Commercial Use Toolkit for Canva Sellers
pages.value: A practical first-pass decision guide for digital product sellers, creators, and small businesses working out what they can actually publish.
pages.quote: Know what you used, know what you’re selling, verify before you list it.

pages.title: How to use this toolkit
pages.lead: Use this as a decision aid, not as a substitute for the current official license terms. Every verdict is a first-pass signal, never a guarantee.

steps.title: Identify
steps.text: Identify the source and label of every asset (open its source info via the ⋯ menu).

steps.title: Define the deliverable
steps.text: Confirm whether the buyer receives a finished product, physical item, or editable/source file.

steps.title: Test the risk
steps.text: Check standalone extractability, the most restrictive content label, and your sales platform’s own rules (e.g. Etsy).

callout.label: FAST RULE
callout.text: A finished design and an editable template are not the same licensing problem.

legend.label: GREEN-LEANING
legend.text: Likely fits the license as described

steps.title: Question 1
steps.text: What did I use — and what label does each item carry?

steps.title: Question 3
steps.text: What files or rights does the buyer receive?

steps.title: Question 4
steps.text: Can any Canva Content be extracted or reused standalone?

steps.title: Question 5
steps.text: Which label is most restrictive — and which account and plan did I export from?

steps.title: Question A
steps.text: Does the design contain Canva library Content (including a Canva template)?

steps.title: Question B
steps.text: Is any item labelled Education (“Resource”), Branded, Disney, or Editorial Use Only?

steps.title: Question C
steps.text: Is any item Pro (crown icon on the thumbnail)?

steps.title: Question D
steps.text: Will the buyer receive an editable template or source file?

steps.title: Question E
steps.text: Could the buyer extract any Canva item as a standalone file?

callout.label: IF B OR E = YES — RED
callout.text: B = not licensed for commercial use (CLA §5B–5D, §9). E = prohibited extraction (CLA §9). Redesign with assets you own or can redistribute. If C and D are both YES: Pro may ship only as a Canva template link (Licensing Explained).

legend.label: GREEN-LEANING
legend.text: Likely fits the license as described

pages.title: Finished products vs. editable products

rows.label: GREEN-LEANING · A REAL DESIGN, NOT ONE ITEM
AMBER · PRO ONLY VIA A CANVA LINK
RED · NOT PERMITTED FOR CANVA CONTENT

pages.note: Flattening alone does not stop extraction (CLA §9). Pro in a PPTX, PSD or other non-Canva template = RED (Licensing Explained). CC0/Pixabay/Pexels items: check their own license.

pages.title: Read the label before you design
pages.lead: Hover over an item, click the three dots (⋯) and read its source information. If a design mixes labels, the most restrictive one applies to the entire design (CLA §1): Education → Branded → Pro → Free.

cards.label: FREE · PRO (CROWN ICON)
cards.text:
Free — GREEN-LEANING · Extra template and resale-template rights (CLA §6), lost if the design contains any Pro.
Pro (crown icon) — GREEN-LEANING in finished designs · Templates: Canva link only · Never standalone (CLA §3; Licensing Explained).

cards.label: AI-GENERATED · CC0 / PUBLIC DOMAIN / PIXABAY / PEXELS
cards.text:
AI-generated — Follows its Free or Pro label (CLA §3A).
CC0 / Public Domain / Pixabay / Pexels — Check that item’s own license (CLA §2, §9).

cards.label: EDUCATION · BRANDED · DISNEY · EDITORIAL · POPULAR MUSIC
cards.text:
Education (“Resource” badge) — RED · Non-commercial use only (CLA §5C).
Branded — RED · Personal use only unless its source info says otherwise (CLA §5B).
Disney — RED · Personal or educational use only (CLA §5D).
Editorial Use Only — RED · No commercial, promotional or merchandising use (CLA §9).
Popular Music — RED · “Can’t be used for any commercial purposes” (Licensing Explained).

cards.label: CANVA LIBRARY TEMPLATE
cards.text: Canva library template — AMBER · It is Content itself: a lightly edited copy is not your template to resell (CLA §1, §3).

callout.label: WHEN THE LICENSE STARTS
callout.text: A license is issued when you Export. One Pro license covers one design; a new or Magic Resized design needs a new one (CLA §4). Pro plans get these automatically; free users pay per item. Attribution: Licensing Explained says none is required, but CLA §9 requires “[Contributor’s Name] via Canva.com” for editorial use. The sources differ, so credit editorial uses.

pages.title: Know the rules before you list it

cards.label: CASE 05 · KNOW YOUR CONTENT
cards.text: Each Canva item carries a label with its own rules. Under CLA §1, the most restrictive category applies to the entire design. From most to least restrictive: Education, Branded, Pro, Free.
cards.note: Verified 25 Sep 2026 · Re-check before you publish

cards.label: CASE 06 · FREE VS. PRO
cards.text: Free Content has extra rights under CLA §6, including templates for distribution or sale. If a design contains any Pro Content, those §6 rights do not apply to that design. Pro Content may never be copied or distributed as a standalone item (CLA §3).
cards.note: Verified 25 Sep 2026 · Re-check before you publish

cards.label: CASE 07 · FINISHED VS. EDITABLE
cards.text: A flattened PDF, image, printed item and editable template are different licensing situations. Canva defines a template as “a design that has a pre-determined layout and style and is intended to be further edited or customised by another person” (Licensing Explained). FINISHED means the buyer receives the final output.

cards.label: CASE 08 · TEMPLATE RULES
cards.signal_label: AMBER · PRO ONLY VIA A CANVA LINK
cards.text: Pro Content may appear only in templates made for use on Canva (CLA §5; Licensing Explained). Templates in any other format (PPTX, PSD, etc.) may contain Free Content only (CLA §6). Canva fonts cannot be used outside Canva (CLA §9A).

pages.title: Know the rules before you list it

cards.label: CASE 09 · MERCHANDISE & POD
cards.signal_label: GREEN-LEANING · A REAL DESIGN, NOT ONE ITEM
cards.text: Designs printed on t-shirts, mugs, books and other merchandise for sale are permitted (Licensing Explained FAQ). A Canva item used on its own, “without any other design elements”, cannot be sold on print-on-demand products (CLA §9).

cards.label: CASE 10 · EBOOKS & PDFS
cards.text: Books, ebooks and electronic publications are permitted uses (CLA §5). In digital publications, each unedited Pro media file is capped at 480,000 total pixels, e.g. 600 × 800 px (CLA §5A). Printed books have no pixel cap.
cards.note: Verified 25 Sep 2026 · Re-check before you publish

cards.label: CASE 11 · CLIENT WORK
cards.text: You may transfer a design containing Free or Pro Content to a single client, under a written agreement limiting use to that client. You remain solely responsible for their compliance. Never hand over standalone Canva Content (CLA §4A).
cards.note: Verified 25 Sep 2026 · Re-check before you publish

pages.title: Know the rules before you list it

cards.label: CASE 12 · LOGOS & TRADEMARKS
cards.text: Licensing Explained says you “cannot use any Free or Pro content from Canva’s library in a trademark (except for fonts, simple shapes and lines)”. The binding CLA §9 excludes only fonts. The sources differ, so the safest logo uses Canva fonts plus graphics you made or commissioned.

cards.label: CASE 13 · EDUCATION, BRANDED & SPECIAL LABELS
cards.text: Education (“Resource” badge): non-commercial only (§5C). Branded: personal use only unless its source info says otherwise (§5B). Disney: no commercial use (§5D). Editorial Use Only: no commercial use (§9). Pro used on an Education account is non-commercial (§8).
cards.note: Verified 25 Sep 2026. For commercial work, CLA §8 says use a separate account; Licensing Explained says a second team. The sources differ.

cards.label: CASE 14 · AI-GENERATED CONTENT
cards.text: Canva’s library AI Content is marked Free or Pro and follows that label’s rules (CLA §3A). Output from Canva’s AI tools is covered by separate AI Product Terms (Terms of Use §6); read them before selling. No Content may be used for AI or machine-learning purposes (CLA §9).
cards.note: Verified 25 Sep 2026. Selling on Etsy? Disclose AI use (see Etsy page).

items.title: Printable planner PDF
items.why: A finished PDF is a permitted electronic publication (CLA §5).
checks: Etsy: my original design, not a PDF of others’ work
items.change: AMBER if unedited Pro images exceed 480,000 px or can be pulled out as files (§5A, §9). RED with any Education, Branded or Disney item, or a page that is just one library image.

items.title: Editable planner template
items.why: Template rights depend on format and labels (CLA §5, §6; Licensing Explained).
checks: Etsy: my own layout, not an edited Canva template
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if delivered only as a Canva template link. RED if it contains Pro and ships in another format, or if it is a resold Canva library template.

items.title: T-shirt design
items.why: Merchandise with your design on it is permitted (Licensing Explained FAQ).
checks: Etsy: disclose production partner + ship-from location
items.change: RED if the shirt is one Canva item with no other design elements (CLA §9), or uses Branded or Disney Content. AMBER if it shows real people, brands or artworks (no releases, CLA §12).

items.title: Mug design
items.why: Same as T-shirts, a genuine design on a product is permitted (Licensing Explained FAQ).
checks: Etsy: disclose production partner + ship-from location
items.change: RED if a single library item is simply placed on the mug (CLA §9) or it uses Branded or Disney Content (§5B, §5D).

items.title: Ebook cover
items.why: Books and book covers are permitted uses (CLA §5).
checks: Etsy: premade covers are my original designs
items.change: AMBER if you sell premade covers to authors (one design per client with written terms, CLA §4A, or a Canva template link). RED if the cover art becomes an author or series logo (CLA §9).

items.title: Ebook interior
items.why: Ebooks are permitted electronic publications (CLA §5).
checks: Etsy: the book is my own work, not someone else’s PDF
items.change: AMBER if an unedited Pro image exceeds 480,000 total pixels per file, e.g. 600 × 800 px (§5A). RED if images can be extracted as reusable files (§9).

items.title: Client Instagram pack
items.why: CLA §4A lets you transfer a design to one client under a written agreement, with you responsible for their compliance.
items.change: RED if the same pack goes to more than one client (that makes it a template) or you hand over standalone Content.

items.title: Logo for a client
items.why: No Free or Pro library content may be used in a trademark (Licensing Explained; CLA §9).
items.change: GREEN-LEANING only with Canva fonts plus your own or commissioned graphics. Simple shapes and lines: allowed by Licensing Explained, not CLA §9. Never promise exclusivity.

items.title: Canva template with Free Content
items.why: CLA §6 lets Free Content be used in templates for sale; a Canva template link is the cleanest delivery.
checks: Etsy: my own original template design
items.change: AMBER in other formats (files may be extractable, §9; fonts can’t leave Canva, §9A). RED if any item is really Pro, Branded or Education.

items.title: Canva template with Pro Content
items.why: Pro may appear only in templates made for use on Canva (Licensing Explained; CLA §5).
checks: Listing says Pro elements need Canva Pro
items.change: RED in any non-Canva format (PPTX, PSD, editable PDF). With a Canva link, tell buyers: “Pro elements show a watermark on free plans; buyers need Canva Pro or a one-off license.”

items.title: Standalone stock photo printable
items.why: Selling a Canva item on its own is prohibited (CLA §3, §9; Licensing Explained “Don’t resell, redistribute”).
checks: Etsy: a PDF of someone else’s work doesn’t qualify
items.change: Only if the item is CC0, Pixabay or Pexels and its own license allows it. Check that license (CLA §9).

items.title: Social media post for own business
items.why: Social media and promotion are permitted uses (CLA §5).
items.change: RED for images of people in tobacco, dating, political or health/supplement ads (§9); Pro Music in paid TV, radio, podcast or billboard ads (§7). RED for Popular Music in any commercial use (Licensing Explained).

items.title: Course workbook PDF
items.why: A finished publication is a permitted use (CLA §5).
items.change: RED if it was made with Pro on a Canva Education account (§8) or contains Education (“Resource”) items (§5C). AMBER if unedited Pro images exceed 480,000 px (§5A).

items.title: Lead magnet PDF
items.why: Promotional materials are permitted (CLA §5), and free distribution follows the same rules as paid.
checks: Same checks as a paid PDF
items.change: AMBER if unedited Pro images exceed 480,000 px or can be extracted (§5A, §9). RED with Branded, Education or Disney items.

items.title: PLR/MRR bundle
items.why: PLR/MRR grants resale or sublicensing rights, which CLA §9 and Terms of Use §2e(i) prohibit for Canva Content. Breaches of those use restrictions fall outside Canva’s liability cap (ToU §14).
checks: Etsy: bundles of others’ work don’t qualify
items.change: Only after replacing all Canva Content with assets you own.

items.title: Presentation template
items.why: Same template rules as Scenario 02 (CLA §5, §6; Licensing Explained).
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if delivered as a Canva template link. RED if Pro Content ships as PPTX, Keynote or Google Slides, or any item is Education or Branded.

items.title: Website graphic
items.why: Web pages are permitted electronic publications (CLA §5).
items.change: AMBER if an unedited Pro image exceeds 480,000 px per file. There is no cap on Canva Websites or embedded Canva designs (§5A). RED if the site offers Content for download (§9).

items.title: Business card template
items.why: CLA §6 names “business card templates” as an allowed use of Free Content.
checks: Etsy: my own original card layout
items.change: AMBER if it contains Pro (Canva link only; buyers may need Pro). RED if Pro ships in another format (Licensing Explained) or it is a resold Canva library template.

items.title: Printed book
items.why: Books are permitted uses, and print is not subject to the §5A pixel cap (CLA §5).
checks: Etsy: disclose print partner if third-party printed
items.change: The ebook edition follows Scenario 06. RED with any Branded, Education or Disney item.

items.title: Digital sticker pack
items.why: Delivering individual Canva graphics as separate files is standalone redistribution (CLA §3, §9; Licensing Explained).
checks: Etsy: stickers are my original designs
items.change: GREEN-LEANING only if every sticker is your own artwork, drawn by you or commissioned with rights.

pages.title: Pre-publish checklist
items: I identified every asset and removed any I can’t trace.
I opened the source info (⋯) and label of every Canva item.
I know whether the buyer receives a finished output or editable/source file.
No Canva item can be extracted as a file or sold on its own.
No item is Education, Branded, Disney or Editorial Use Only.
Unedited Pro media is ≤ 480,000 px; Pro templates ship only as Canva links.
I exported with an active Pro plan (or paid per Pro item) on a non-Education account.
I checked the current official terms, not old articles or other listings, and saved the date.
I checked my platform’s rules (Etsy: original design, partner and AI disclosure).
No PLR/MRR/resale rights promised, and my buyer Read Me says so.

pages.title: Stop before you publish
items: You are selling a Canva item on its own, without other design elements.
Your editable template contains Pro Content but relies on Free Content’s additional template permissions.
You cannot identify the source of an image, icon, font, or illustration.
You use another seller’s listing as proof that a use is permitted.
You promise PLR, MRR, resale, or sublicensing rights over content you do not own.
You use Education, Branded, Disney or “Editorial Use Only” Content in anything commercial or promotional.
The product’s real value is effectively giving the buyer access to the original Canva asset.

callout.label: SIMPLIFY BEFORE YOU SELL
callout.text: If the licensing story requires a chain of assumptions, simplify the product before you sell it.

pages.title: Etsy checks & what’s at stake
pages.lead: Canva’s license and your marketplace’s rules are two separate tests. Pass both. (Etsy Creativity Standards, last updated 10 June 2025.)

cards.label: ETSY — FIVE CHECKS · 1–2
cards.text:
1. Original design. Canva-made downloads and print-on-demand items fall under “Designed by a seller”: they must be your original designs. “A bundle, collection, scan, or PDF of someone else’s work” does not qualify, and that includes unmodified Canva templates or library graphics.
2. Production partner. Printed by a third party (POD shirts, mugs, books)? Disclose the production partner and where the item ships from.

cards.label: ETSY — FIVE CHECKS · 3–5
cards.text:
3. AI disclosure. Made with AI tools? Say so in the listing description. Our cautious reading: also disclose Canva library items marked AI-generated.
4. Personalised items. For custom items, the first image must show a finished, customised item, not placeholder text like “Your Text Here”.
5. Removal. Etsy may remove listings that break its policies, and listing fees remain payable.

cards.label: WHAT’S AT STAKE ON CANVA’S SIDE · 1–2
cards.text:
Canva may delete designs, suspend or terminate your account, or permanently ban you (Terms of Use §15b).
After termination for a violation: no refund, and no new account without Canva’s written permission (ToU §15c).

cards.label: WHAT’S AT STAKE ON CANVA’S SIDE · 3–4
cards.text:
If your license ends, you must stop using and delete the Content and designs (CLA §10).
Breaching the “Restrictions on Use of the Service” is excluded from the liability cap, and you indemnify Canva (ToU §13–14).

callout.label: GUMROAD · BEACONS
callout.text: Selling on Gumroad, Beacons or elsewhere? Check that platform’s own rules separately.

pages.lead: Use this page only to describe rights you actually control in your original material. Canva Content inside your product stays under Canva’s license; you cannot grant rights over it.
fields: WHAT MAY THE BUYER NOT DO?

pages.title: A safer product-building hierarchy
pages.lead: Move from clearer rights at the top toward higher-friction situations at the bottom.

levels.label: LOWER FRICTION
levels.text: Original text + original graphics + your own photos/illustrations

levels.label: LOWER FRICTION
levels.text: Original layout + external assets with clear commercial/redistribution rights

levels.label: GREEN-LEANING
levels.text: Finished designs using Canva Free/Pro Content within permitted uses (CLA §5)

levels.label: AMBER
levels.text: Editable templates: Free-only, or Pro delivered only as a Canva link

levels.label: RED
levels.text: Pro in non-Canva template formats, or any Education, Branded or Disney Content in a product for sale

levels.label: AVOID
levels.text: Treating Canva Content itself as a resellable or sublicensable asset
